A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Soft Quality-Diversity Optimization and contain readable main text and Appendices A–G. Their equations, experiments, tables, and figures can be reliably matched despite formatting and pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original SQUAD experiments on Linear Projection, Image Composition, and Latent Space Illumination, together with appendix ablations and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, qualitative examples, and runtime measurements in Section 5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Equations 2–5 and Algorithm 1 retain the same objective, pairwise approximation, gradient updates, nearest-neighbor computation, minibatches, and logit transformation. Algorithm 1 is relocated without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Linear Projection with 4-, 8-, and 16-dimensional behavior spaces, five-dimensional Image Composition, and the two- and seven-dimensional LSI tasks. Appendix D.1 retains the same targets and behavior descriptors.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain CMA-MAEGA, CMA-MEGA, Sep-CMA-MAE, GA-ME, DNS, and DNS-G. The qualitative comparisons also retain the same two CMA baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix D retain the same metrics, CVT archive sizes, tuning procedures, population and batch sizes, and training budgets. No experimental setting or evaluation procedure is revised.

E4.justification: The bandwidth study in Figure 4, four Appendix C ablations, qualitative and archive comparisons, and Appendix G runtime and convergence analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain 10 runs for LP/IC, five for LSI, and the same ablation seed counts. Mean-and-standard-error reporting and the Kruskal–Wallis and Holm–Bonferroni-corrected Mann–Whitney tests remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative samples match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains SQUAD QVS values of 177.0 ± 2.8 for base LSI and 151.3 ± 0.1 for hard LSI.

T1.justification: The Soft QD definitions, lower-bound derivation, approximation-error analysis, and monotonicity, submodularity, and limiting-equivalence proofs are unchanged, including Appendices A and B.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about discretization-free Soft QD, differentiable SQUAD, competitive performance, and scalability to higher-dimensional behavior spaces.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations concerning differentiability, bandwidth selection, omitted higher-order interactions, and bounded-space transformations are retained. Added citations support existing future-work suggestions without changing their substance.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit source-code repository URL in the abstract and an experiment-code hyperlink in Section 5. v1 only refers to accompanying code in Appendix D.3. Implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and runtime details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Spielman and Srivastava (2011), Graph Sparsification by Effective Resistances, to support the existing sparsification suggestion. It also cites the already-referenced Zhuo et al. (2018) in that future-work passage. The broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 8 acknowledgments and funding disclosure, updates affiliations and publication-status text, and changes heading and citation styles. The scientific prose and section sequence are otherwise substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The ICLR template changes the title/author layout, running headers, typography, spacing, and float placement. Algorithm 1 moves from page 6 to 5 and Table 2 from page 9 to 8; existing figure content and table organization are retained.

improvement.justification: Explicit code links improve access information over v1's generic reference to accompanying code, while the added citations and funding disclosure modestly improve documentation and transparency. The method, proofs, and empirical evidence remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
